ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْنَاهُ نَعْمَاءَ بَعْدَ ضَرَّاءَ مَسَّتْهُ لَيَقُولَنَّ ذَهَبَ السَّيِّئَاتُ عَنِّي إِنَّهُ لَفَرِحٌ فَخُورٌ (١٠))
His saying (لَفَرِحٌ): it is read with kasra on the rāʾ and with ḍamma; they are two dialectal forms, like يَقُظٌ and يَقِظٌ, and حَذُرٌ and حَذِرٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ كَبِيرٌ (١١))
His saying (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا): in the position of the accusative; it is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil), and that from which the exception is made is الْإِنْسَانُ ("man").
It is also said: it is disconnected (munfaṣil). It is also said: it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ» is its khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَعَلَّكَ تَارِكٌ بَعْضَ مَا يُوحَى إِلَيْكَ وَضَائِقٌ بِهِ صَدْرُكَ أَنْ يَقُولُوا لَوْلَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ كَنْزٌ أَوْ جَاءَ مَعَهُ مَلَكٌ إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ نَذِيرٌ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَكِيلٌ (١٢))
His saying (وَضَائِقٌ بِهِ صَدْرُكَ): صَدْرُكَ is made nominative by ضَائِقٌ, because it leans on the mubtadaʾ (subject). It is also said: it is a mubtadaʾ, and ضَائِقٌ is a khabar (predicate) placed before it. «ضَائِقٌ» came on the pattern fāʿil from ضَاقَ يَضِيقُ. (أَنْ يَقُولُوا): i.e. "for fear that they say". It is also said: "because they say", i.e. "because they said", so it has the meaning of the past.

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَيْسَ لَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا النَّارُ وَحَبِطَ مَا صَنَعُوا فِيهَا وَبَاطِلٌ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ (١٦))
His saying (وَبَاطِلٌ): a khabar (predicate) placed first, and «مَا كَانُوا» is the mubtadaʾ (subject); the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. يَعْمَلُونَهُ ("they used to do it"). It was also read بَاطِلًا in the accusative; the governing word in it is «يَعْمَلُونَ», and مَا is redundant (zāʾida).

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَفَمَنْ كَانَ عَلَى بَيِّنَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَيَتْلُوهُ شَاهِدٌ مِنْهُ وَمِنْ قَبْلِهِ كِتَابُ مُوسَى إِمَامًا وَرَحْمَةً أُولَئِكَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِهِ مِنَ الْأَحْزَابِ فَالنَّارُ مَوْعِدُهُ فَلَا تَكُ فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِنْهُ إِنَّهُ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ (١٧))
His saying (أَفَمَنْ كَانَ): in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: "Is the one who is upon these things like someone else?"
(وَيَتْلُوهُ): concerning the hāʾ there are several views.
The first: it refers back to «مَنْ», who is the Prophet ﷺ, and the implied form is: "and there follows Muhammad", i.e. the truthfulness of Muhammad. (شَاهِدٌ مِنْهُ): i.e. his tongue. It is also said: the witness is Jibrīl, peace be upon him. The hāʾ in (مِنْهُ) refers to Allah, and in «مِنْ قَبْلِهِ» to the Prophet.
And «كِتَابُ مُوسَى» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the witness. It is also said: the witness is the Gospel, and the meaning is that the Torah and the Gospel follow Muhammad ﷺ in confirming him; and He separated the conjunction from the conjoined with His saying «مِنْ قَبْلِهِ», i.e. "and the Book of Mūsā, peace be upon him, before it". The second view: the hāʾ refers to the Qurʾān, i.e. "and there follows the Qurʾān a witness from Muhammad ﷺ", which is his tongue. It is also said: Jibrīl, peace be upon him. The third: it refers back to the clear statement (al-bayān) indicated by «الْبَيِّنَةُ». It is also said: the sentence is complete at His saying «مِنْهُ», and «وَمِنْ قَبْلِهِ كِتَابُ مُوسَى», peace be upon him, is a mubtadaʾ and khabar.
And (إِمَامًا وَرَحْمَةً): two ḥāls (circumstantials).
It was also read «كِتَابَ مُوسَى» in the accusative, i.e. "and he recites the Book of Mūsā".
(فِي مِرْيَةٍ): it is read with kasra and with ḍamma, and they are two dialectal forms.

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا اللَّهَ إِنَّنِي لَكُمْ مِنْهُ نَذِيرٌ وَبَشِيرٌ (٢))
His saying (أَنْ لَا تَعْبُدُوا): concerning «أَنْ» there are three views. The first: it is lightened from the heavy (form) [Translator's note: i.e. أَنْ lightened from أَنَّ].
The second: it is the one that puts the verb in the accusative (al-nāṣiba). On both views its position is nominative, the implied form being: «هِيَ أَنْ لَا تَعْبُدُوا» ("it is: that you worship none…"). It may also be that the implied form is «بِأَنْ لَا تَعْبُدُوا» ("with: that you worship none…"), so that its position is genitive or accusative, according to the disagreement we have related. The third view: «أَنْ» has the meaning of أَيْ (explicative "that is"), so it has no grammatical position, and «وَلَا تَعْبُدُوا» is a prohibition.
And (مِنْهُ): i.e. from Allah. The implied form is «نَذِيرٌ كَائِنٌ مِنْهُ» ("a warner being from Him"); when He placed it first, it became a ḥāl (circumstantial).
It may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to نَذِيرٍ, the implied form being: "I am to you a warner on account of His punishment."

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أُولَئِكَ لَمْ يَكُونُوا مُعْجِزِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا كَانَ لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ أَوْلِيَاءَ يُضَاعَفُ لَهُمُ الْعَذَابُ مَا كَانُوا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ السَّمْعَ وَمَا كَانُوا يُبْصِرُونَ (٢٠))
His saying (يُضَاعَفُ لَهُمُ): resumptive (mustaʾnaf).
(مَا كَانُوا): concerning (مَا) there are three views:
The first: it has the meaning of الَّذِي (relative noun), and the meaning is "it is multiplied for them because of what they used to…"; when the preposition was omitted, it was made accusative. The second: it is maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar), and the implied form is "for the duration that they were able". The third: it is negating, i.e. out of the intensity of their hatred for it they were not able to listen to it.

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا جَرَمَ أَنَّهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ هُمُ الْأَخْسَرُونَ (٢٢))
His saying (لَا جَرَمَ): concerning it there are four opinions. The first: (لَا) is a rejection of preceding speech, i.e. "the matter is not as they claimed", and (جَرَمَ) is a verb whose fāʿil (agent) is implied within it.
And (أَنَّهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ) is in the position of the accusative, the implied form being: "their saying has earned them their loss in the Hereafter." The second opinion: (لَا جَرَمَ) are two words that were compounded and came to mean "truly" (حَقًّا), and «أَنَّـ…» is in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of حَقَّ, i.e. "their loss is a certainty". The third: the meaning is "inevitably (لَا مَحَالَةَ) is their loss", so it is also in the position of the nominative. It is also said: in the position of the accusative or the genitive, since the implied form is "there is no avoiding their loss". The fourth: the meaning is "there is nothing preventing that they have lost", so in its i'rab it is like the one before it.

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَثَلُ الْفَرِيقَيْنِ كَالْأَعْمَى وَالْأَصَمِّ وَالْبَصِيرِ وَالسَّمِيعِ هَلْ يَسْتَوِيَانِ مَثَلًا أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ (٢٤))
His saying (مَثَلُ الْفَرِيقَيْنِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is «كَالْأَعْمَى», the implied form being "like the likeness of the blind". One of the two parties is the blind and the deaf, and the other is the seeing and the hearing.
(مَثَلًا): a tamyīz (specification).

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَى قَوْمِهِ إِنِّي لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ (٢٥))
His saying (إِنِّي لَكُمْ): it is read with kasra on the hamza, on the implied form "so he said: indeed I…"; and with fatḥa on it, on the implied form "with (the message) that I…" (بِأَنِّي), and it is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "We sent him with the warning", i.e. as a warner.

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَنْ لَا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا اللَّهَ إِنِّي أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ (٢٦))
His saying (أَنْ لَا تَعْبُدُوا): it is like the one at the beginning of the sūra.

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَقَالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ مَا نَرَاكَ إِلَّا بَشَرًا مِثْلَنَا وَمَا نَرَاكَ اتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ هُمْ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِيَ الرَّأْيِ وَمَا نَرَى لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا مِنْ فَضْلٍ بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كَاذِبِينَ (٢٧))
His saying (مَا نَرَاكَ): it may be from seeing with the eye, in which case the clause after it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), with «قَدْ» intended along with it.
It may also be from seeing with the heart (cognition), in which case the clause is in the position of the second mafʿūl (object).
And «الْأَرَاذِلُ» is the plural of أَرْذَالٌ, and أَرْذَالٌ is the plural of رَذْلٌ. It is also said: the singular is أَرْذَلُ and the plural أَرَاذِلُ; it was given a plural on this measure even though it is an adjective, because it became predominant and so became like the nouns. The meaning of its predominance is that the thing described is hardly ever mentioned with it; it is like الْأَبْطَحُ and الْأَبْرَقُ.
(بَادِيَ الرَّأْيِ): it is read with a hamza after the dāl, from بَدَأَ يَبْدَأُ, when one does something first. It is also read with a yāʾ with fatḥa, and in this there are two views:
The first: the hamza was replaced by a yāʾ because of the kasra before it. The second: it is from بَدَا يَبْدُو, when something appears.
بَادِيَ here is an adverb (ẓarf); it came on the pattern fāʿil, just as it comes on the pattern faʿīl, such as قَرِيبٌ and بَعِيدٌ; and it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like الْعَافِيَةُ and الْعَاقِبَةُ. Concerning what governs it there are four views. The first: نَرَاكَ, i.e. "in what appears to us of opinion", or "at the first of our opinion".
If it is said: what precedes «إِلَّا», when complete, does not govern what follows it, as in your saying مَا أَعْطَيْتُ أَحَدًا إِلَّا زَيْدًا دِينَارًا ("I gave no one except Zayd a dinar"), because إِلَّا makes the verb transitive, but makes it transitive only to one (word), like the wāw in the chapter of the mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment) — it is said in reply: that is permitted here because «بَادِيَ» is an adverb, or like an adverb, as in جَهْدَ رَأْيِي أَنَّكَ ذَاهِبٌ ("to the utmost of my opinion, you are going"), i.e. فِي جَهْدِ رَأْيِي; and latitude is allowed with adverbs. The second view: what governs it is (اتَّبَعَكَ), i.e. "they followed you at first opinion", or "in what appeared of it, without their investigating". The third view: it belongs to the completion of (أَرَاذِلُنَا), i.e. "the lowest in our opinion". The fourth: what governs it is omitted, i.e. "he says that at first opinion of it".
And (الرَّأْيِ) is read with a hamza and without a hamza.

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُ عَلَى بَيِّنَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّي وَآتَانِي رَحْمَةً مِنْ عِنْدِهِ فَعُمِّيَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنُلْزِمُكُمُوهَا وَأَنْتُمْ لَهَا كَارِهُونَ (٢٨))
His saying (رَحْمَةً مِنْ عِنْدِهِ): «مِنْ» may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb, or it may be part of the naʿt (adjective) of الرَّحْمَةُ.
(فَعَمِيَتْ): i.e. it was hidden from you, because you did not look into it as it deserved. It is also said the meaning is "you were blind to it", like their saying أَدْخَلْتُ الْخَاتَمَ فِي أُصْبُعِي ("I put the ring onto my finger") [Translator's note: i.e. an inverted expression, the finger actually entering the ring].
It is also read with the doubling (shadda) and the ḍamma [Translator's note: i.e. فَعُمِّيَتْ], i.e. it was made obscure to you as a punishment for you.
And (أَنُلْزِمُكُمُوهَا): its past is أَلْزَمْتُ, and it is transitive to two objects. The wāw entered here as a completion of the mīm, and that is the original form of the mīm of the plural.
It was also read with the first mīm made quiescent, to avoid a succession of vowels.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَنِ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ ثُمَّ تُوبُوا إِلَيْهِ يُمَتِّعْكُمْ مَتَاعًا حَسَنًا إِلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى وَيُؤْتِ كُلَّ ذِي فَضْلٍ فَضْلَهُ وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنِّي أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ كَبِيرٍ (٣))
His saying (وَأَنِ اسْتَغْفِرُوا): «أَنْ» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the first «أَنْ», and it is like it in what has been mentioned.
(وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا): i.e. يَتَوَلَّوْا [Translator's note: i.e. it is understood as an imperfect verb, not a past one].

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا أَقُولُ لَكُمْ عِنْدِي خَزَائِنُ اللَّهِ وَلَا أَعْلَمُ الْغَيْبَ وَلَا أَقُولُ إِنِّي مَلَكٌ وَلَا أَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ تَزْدَرِي أَعْيُنُكُمْ لَنْ يُؤْتِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ خَيْرًا اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ إِنِّي إِذًا لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ (٣١))
His saying (تَزْدَرِي): the dāl is a substitute for the tāʾ; its origin is تَزْتَرِي, of the pattern taftaʿil from زَرِيتُ. It was changed into a dāl to match the zāy in voicing (jahr), whereas the tāʾ is unvoiced (mahmūsa), so it could not be combined with the zāy.

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ يَثْنُونَ صُدُورَهُمْ لِيَسْتَخْفُوا مِنْهُ أَلَا حِينَ يَسْتَغْشُونَ ثِيَابَهُمْ يَعْلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ (٥))
His saying (يَثْنُونَ): the majority read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the nūn; its past is ثَنَى.
It is also read the same way except with ḍamma on the yāʾ, its past being أَثْنَى. This is not known in the language, unless it is said that its meaning is "they exposed them to being folded", just as you say أَبَعْتُ الْفَرَسَ when you have offered the horse for sale.
It is also read with the yāʾ with fatḥa, sukūn on the thāʾ, a nūn with fatḥa, followed by a hamza with ḍamma, followed by a doubled nūn with fatḥa, like يَقْرَءُونَ [Translator's note: i.e. يَثْنَؤُنَّ]. It is from ثَنَيْتُ, except that he changed the yāʾ into a wāw because it took ḍamma, then gave it a hamza because it took ḍamma.
It is also read يَثْنَوْنِي, like يَعْشَوْشِبُ; it is of the pattern yafʿawʿil, from ثَنَيْتُ, and الصُّدُورُ is the fāʿil (agent).
It is also read the same way, except with the final yāʾ dropped for lightness because of the length of the word.
It is also read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the nūn, and a hamza with kasra followed by a doubled nūn with ḍamma [Translator's note: i.e. يَثْنَئِنُّ]. The origin of the word is yafʿawʿil from الثَّنْي, except that he replaced the wāw with kasra by a hamza, as it was replaced in وِسَادَةٍ, so that they said إِسَادَةٍ. It is also said that its origin is yafʿāll, like يَحْمَارُّ, and the alif was replaced by a hamza, just as they said ابْيَاضَّ [Translator's note: the example presumably intends the hamzated form ابْيَأَضَّ].
(أَلَا حِينَ): the governing word (ʿāmil) of the adverb (ẓarf) is omitted, i.e. "Indeed, when they cover themselves with their garments, they seek to hide." It may also be an adverb for «يَعْلَمُ».

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا مِنْ دَابَّةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا عَلَى اللَّهِ رِزْقُهَا وَيَعْلَمُ مُسْتَقَرَّهَا وَمُسْتَوْدَعَهَا كُلٌّ فِي كِتَابٍ مُبِينٍ (٦))
His saying (مُسْتَقَرَّهَا وَمُسْتَوْدَعَهَا): two nouns of place. They may also be two maṣdars (verbal nouns), as the poet said:
أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ مُسَرِّحِيَ الْقَوَافِي
(Do you not know my sending forth of rhymes…)
i.e. تَسْرِيحِي ("my sending forth").

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَئِنْ أَخَّرْنَا عَنْهُمُ الْعَذَابَ إِلَى أُمَّةٍ مَعْدُودَةٍ لَيَقُولُنَّ مَا يَحْبِسُهُ أَلَا يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمْ لَيْسَ مَصْرُوفًا عَنْهُمْ وَحَاقَ بِهِمْ مَا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ (٨))
His saying (وَلَئِنْ): the lām is for preparing the oath (tawṭiʾat al-qasam), and the oath is omitted; its answer is «لَيَقُولُنَّ». [And like it is]: (وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْنَا), where the answer of the oath is (إِنَّهُ لَيَئُوسٌ). The oath and its answer stand in place of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
His saying (أَلَا يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمْ): يَوْمَ is an adverb (ẓarf) for «مَصْرُوفًا», i.e. "it will not be turned away from them on the day it comes to them." This shows the permissibility of placing the khabar (predicate) of لَيْسَ before it. Some of them said: the governing word in it is omitted, indicated by the context, i.e. "the punishment will not be turned away from them on the day it comes to them"; and the noun of لَيْسَ is implied within it, i.e. "the punishment is not turned away."

ukberi-tibyan:32-32.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا يَا نُوحُ قَدْ جَادَلْتَنَا فَأَكْثَرْتَ جِدَالَنَا فَأْتِنَا بِمَا تَعِدُنَا إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ (٣٢))
His saying (قَدْ جَادَلْتَنَا): the majority keep the alif, and likewise in «جِدَالَنَا».
It was also read «جَدَلْتَنَا فَأَكْثَرْتَ جَدَلَنَا» without an alif in both, meaning "you have overcome us in disputation".

ukberi-tibyan:34-34.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا يَنْفَعُكُمْ نُصْحِي إِنْ أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَنْصَحَ لَكُمْ إِنْ كَانَ اللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يُغْوِيَكُمْ هُوَ رَبُّكُمْ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ (٣٤))
His saying (إِنْ أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَنْصَحَ لَكُمْ إِنْ كَانَ اللَّهُ): the rule for a condition when it enters upon another condition is that the second condition together with the answer form the answer to the first condition, as in your saying إِنْ أَتَيْتَنِي إِنْ كَلَّمْتَنِي أَكْرَمْتُكَ ("if you come to me, if you speak to me, I will honour you"): your saying إِنْ كَلَّمْتَنِي أَكْرَمْتُكَ is the answer to إِنْ أَتَيْتَنِي. Since that is so, the condition that is first in mention becomes later in meaning, so that if he came to him and then spoke to him, the honouring would not be due; but if he spoke to him and then came to him, honouring him would be due.
The reason for this is that the answer has become held back by the second condition. Of this there has come in the Qurʾān His saying: (إِنْ وَهَبَتْ نَفْسَهَا لِلنَّبِيِّ إِنْ أَرَادَ النَّبِيُّ).

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَرَاهُ قُلْ إِنِ افْتَرَيْتُهُ فَعَلَيَّ إِجْرَامِي وَأَنَا بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تُجْرِمُونَ (٣٥))
His saying (فَعَلَيَّ إِجْرَامِي): it is read with kasra on the hamza, being the maṣdar (verbal noun) of أَجْرَمَ; there is another dialectal form of it: «جَرْمٌ». And with fatḥa on the hamza, being the plural of جُرْمٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأُوحِيَ إِلَى نُوحٍ أَنَّهُ لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ مِنْ قَوْمِكَ إِلَّا مَنْ قَدْ آمَنَ فَلَا تَبْتَئِسْ بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ (٣٦))
His saying (أَنَّهُ لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ): it is read with fatḥa on the hamza, and «أَنَّهُ» is in the position of the nominative by أُوحِيَ (as its nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent).
It is also read with kasra on it, the implied form being "it was said: indeed…", and what is made nominative by أُوحِيَ is (that implied saying).
His saying (إِلَّا مَنْ قَدْ آمَنَ): an exception from outside the genus in meaning, and it is the fāʿil (agent) of «لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ».

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاصْنَعِ الْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا وَلَا تُخَاطِبْنِي فِي الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا إِنَّهُمْ مُغْرَقُونَ (٣٧))
His saying (بِأَعْيُنِنَا): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in «اصْنَعْ», i.e. "being protected".

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ التَّنُّورُ قُلْنَا احْمِلْ فِيهَا مِنْ كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَنْ سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ الْقَوْلُ وَمَنْ آمَنَ وَمَا آمَنَ مَعَهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ (٤٠))
His saying (مِنْ كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ): «كُلِّ» is read with annexation (iḍāfa), and in this there are two views. The first: the mafʿūl (object) of «احْمِلْ» is «اثْنَيْنِ», its implied form being "carry in it two of every pair"; on this view مِنْ is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it is an adjective of an indefinite noun placed before it.
The second: «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), the object is «كُلِّ», and اثْنَيْنِ is a tawkīd (emphasis); this is according to the view of al-Akhfash. «مِنْ كُلٍّ» is also read with tanwīn; on this reading the object of «احْمِلْ» is «زَوْجَيْنِ», and «اثْنَيْنِ» is an emphasis of it; and «مِنْ» on this reading may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to احْمِلْ, or may be a ḥāl; the implied form is "of every thing" or "of every kind".
(وَأَهْلَكَ) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the object.
And (إِلَّا مَنْ سَبَقَ) is a connected exception.
(وَمَنْ آمَنَ): also an object of احْمِلْ.

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ ارْكَبُوا فِيهَا بِسْمِ اللَّهِ مَجْرَاهَا وَمُرْسَاهَا إِنَّ رَبِّي لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (٤١))
His saying (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ مَجْرَاهَا): مَجْرَاهَا is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and بِسْمِ اللَّهِ is its khabar (predicate); the clause is an anticipated ḥāl (circumstantial, ḥāl muqaddara), and the one it describes is the wāw in «ارْكَبُوا».
It is also permissible for مَجْرَاهَا to be made nominative by بِسْمِ اللَّهِ, on the basis that «بِسْمِ اللَّهِ» is a ḥāl from the wāw in ارْكَبُوا. It is also permissible for the clause to be a ḥāl from the hāʾ, its implied form being "ride in it, while its course is in the name of Allah"; and it too is anticipated. It is also said: مَجْرَاهَا and مُرْسَاهَا are two adverbs of place, and بِسْمِ اللَّهِ is a ḥāl from the wāw, i.e. "naming (Allah) at the place of its sailing".
It may also be (an adverb of) time, i.e. "at the time of its sailing".
It is also read with ḍamma on the mīm in both, being the maṣdar of أَجْرَيْتُ مُجْرًى; and with fatḥa on both, being the maṣdar of جَرَيْتُ and رَسَيْتُ.
It is also read with ḍamma on the mīm, kasra on the rāʾ and the sīn and a yāʾ after them [Translator's note: i.e. مُجْرِيهَا وَمُرْسِيهَا], and it is then an adjective of the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهِيَ تَجْرِي بِهِمْ فِي مَوْجٍ كَالْجِبَالِ وَنَادَى نُوحٌ ابْنَهُ وَكَانَ فِي مَعْزِلٍ يَا بُنَيَّ ارْكَبْ مَعَنَا وَلَا تَكُنْ مَعَ الْكَافِرِينَ (٤٢))
His saying (وَهِيَ تَجْرِي بِهِمْ): the clause may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in بِسْمِ اللَّهِ, i.e. "its course is in the name of Allah, while it sails with them".
It may also be resumptive (mustaʾnafa), with «بِهِمْ» a ḥāl from the pronoun in تَجْرِي, i.e. "while they are in it".
(نُوحٌ ابْنَهُ): the majority read it with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, which is the original.
It was also read with the ḥāʾ quiescent, treating continuous speech like a pause.
It is also read ابْنَهَا, meaning the son of his wife; as though he (the reader) understood it to be annexed to her rather than to him, because of His saying: (إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ). It is also read with fatḥa on the hāʾ without an alif; the alif was dropped for lightness and the fatḥa indicates it; like it is «يَا أَبَتَ» in the reading of those who give it fatḥa.
It is also read «ابْنَاهُ» as an expression of lamentation (tarathhī), and it is not a nudba (lament with وَا) because the nudba is not made with the hamza [Translator's note: i.e. with the vocative particle أَ / يَا rather than وَا, as the source puts it].
(فِي مَعْزِلٍ): with kasra on the zāy it is a place, not a maṣdar (verbal noun); with fatḥa on it, it is a maṣdar; and I do not know of anyone who read it with fatḥa.
(يَا بُنَيَّ): it is read with kasra on the yāʾ. Its origin is بُنَيٌّ, with the yāʾ of the diminutive and a yāʾ that is the final radical (lām) of the word, whose origin is a wāw according to some and a yāʾ according to others; the third yāʾ is the yāʾ of the speaker, but it was dropped because the kasra indicates it, to avoid a succession of yāʾs, and because the vocative is a place of lightening. It is also said: it was dropped from pronunciation because of its meeting with the rāʾ in «ارْكَبْ».
It is also read with fatḥa, and in this there are two views. The first: he replaced the kasra by a fatḥa, so the yāʾ of annexation turned (into an alif), then the alif was dropped just as the yāʾ is dropped with the kasra, because it is its origin. The second: the alif was dropped from pronunciation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ سَآوِي إِلَى جَبَلٍ يَعْصِمُنِي مِنَ الْمَاءِ قَالَ لَا عَاصِمَ الْيَوْمَ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ وَحَالَ بَيْنَهُمَا الْمَوْجُ فَكَانَ مِنَ الْمُغْرَقِينَ (٤٣))
His saying (لَا عَاصِمَ الْيَوْمَ): in it there are three views:
The first: it is an active participle in its proper sense. On this view, His saying (إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ) has two possibilities. The first: it is a connected exception, and «مَنْ رَحِمَ» has the meaning of "the one who shows mercy", i.e. "there is no protector except Allah". The second: it is disconnected, i.e. "but whomever Allah has mercy on is protected".
The second view: عَاصِمٌ has the meaning of مَعْصُومٌ ("protected"), like (مَاءٍ دَافِقٍ), i.e. مَدْفُوقٌ ("poured"); on this view the exception is connected, i.e. "except whomever Allah has mercy on". The third: عَاصِمٌ has the meaning of "possessed of protection", by way of relation (nasab), like حَائِضٌ and طَالِقٌ; on this view too the exception is connected. As for the khabar (predicate) of «لَا», it cannot be «الْيَوْمَ», because an adverb of time cannot be a predicate of a concrete entity; rather the khabar is «مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ», and «الْيَوْمَ» is governed by «مِنْ أَمْرِ». Nor can الْيَوْمَ be governed by عَاصِمٌ, since if it were so it would have been given tanwīn.

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقِيلَ يَا أَرْضُ ابْلَعِي مَاءَكِ وَيَا سَمَاءُ أَقْلِعِي وَغِيضَ الْمَاءُ وَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ وَاسْتَوَتْ عَلَى الْجُودِيِّ وَقِيلَ بُعْدًا لِلْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ (٤٤))
His saying (عَلَى الْجُودِيِّ): with the yāʾ doubled, which is the original.
It was also read with it lightened (undoubled), because the two yāʾs are felt to be heavy.
(وَغِيضَ الْمَاءُ): this verb is used intransitively and transitively. Of the transitive is «وَغِيضَ الْمَاءُ», and of the intransitive is (وَمَا تَغِيضُ الْأَرْحَامُ).
It is also possible that this too is transitive; one says غَاضَ الْمَاءُ ("the water sank") and غُضْتُهُ ("I made it sink") [Translator's note: the source as printed reads «وَغْضَتَهُ»; the intended form is presumably غُضْتُهُ].
And (بُعْدًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "and it was said: may they be far removed (بَعُدَ بُعْدًا)".
And (لِلْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ): clarification and specification; the lām is not attached (mutaʿalliq) to the maṣdar.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ يَا نُوحُ إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ إِنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صَالِحٍ فَلَا تَسْأَلْنِي مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ إِنِّي أَعِظُكَ أَنْ تَكُونَ مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ (٤٦))
His saying (إِنَّهُ عَمَلٌ): concerning the hāʾ there are three views. The first: it is the pronoun of the son, i.e. "he is a possessor of (unrighteous) deeds". The second: it is the pronoun of the calling and the asking concerning his son, i.e. "your asking concerning him is an unrighteous deed". The third: it is the pronoun of the riding, which «ارْكَبْ مَعَنَا» indicated.
Whoever read «عَمِلَ» as a past verb, the hāʾ is the pronoun of the son and nothing else.
(فَلَا تَسْأَلْنِي): it is read with the yāʾ kept, according to the original, and with it dropped for lightness, the kasra indicating it.
It is also read with fatḥa on the lām and the nūn doubled, as the nūn of emphasis; some of them give it kasra and some give it fatḥa, and the meaning is clear.

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي أَعُوَذُ بِكَ أَنْ أَسْأَلَكَ مَا لَيْسَ لِي بِهِ عِلْمٌ وَإِلَّا تَغْفِرْ لِي وَتَرْحَمْنِي أَكُنْ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ (٤٧))
His saying (وَإِلَّا تَغْفِرْ لِي): the jussive is by إِنْ, and its governing effect is not cancelled by لَا, because «لَا» has become like a part of the verb; it does not govern in negation, and it negates what is in the future. «مَا» is not like that, for it negates what is in the present; for that reason «إِنْ» may not enter upon it, because the conditional إِنْ is specific to the future, whereas «مَا» is for negating the present.

ukberi-tibyan:48-48.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قِيلَ يَا نُوحُ اهْبِطْ بِسَلَامٍ مِنَّا وَبَرَكَاتٍ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَى أُمَمٍ مِمَّنْ مَعَكَ وَأُمَمٌ سَنُمَتِّعُهُمْ ثُمَّ يَمَسُّهُمْ مِنَّا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (٤٨))
His saying (قِيلَ يَا نُوحُ): «يَا» and «نُوحُ» are in the position of the nominative because they occupy the place of the fāʿil (agent) [Translator's note: i.e. of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the passive قِيلَ]. It is also said: what stands in place of the agent is an implied pronoun, and the vocative explains it, i.e. "a saying was said", or "it was said, namely: O Nūḥ".
(بِسَلَامٍ مِنَّا): two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the agent pronoun.
(وَأُمَمٌ): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the pronoun in اهْبِطْ, its implied form being "go down, you and nations"; the separation between the two made a tawkīd (emphasis) unnecessary.
(سَنُمَتِّعُهُمْ): a naʿt (adjective) of أُمَمٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:49-49.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (تِلْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهَا إِلَيْكَ مَا كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُهَا أَنْتَ وَلَا قَوْمُكَ مِنْ قَبْلِ هَذَا فَاصْبِرْ إِنَّ الْعَاقِبَةَ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ (٤٩))
His saying (تِلْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الْغَيْبِ): it is like His saying in Āl ʿImrān: (ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الْغَيْبِ), whose i'rab has already been mentioned.
(مَا كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُهَا): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the feminine pronoun in «نُوحِيهَا», or a ḥāl from the kāf in «إِلَيْكَ».

ukberi-tibyan:50-50.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِلَى عَادٍ أَخَاهُمْ هُودًا قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مَا لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرُهُ إِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا مُفْتَرُونَ (٥٠))
His saying (مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرُهُ): this has been mentioned in al-Aʿrāf.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَا قَوْمِ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ ثُمَّ تُوبُوا إِلَيْهِ يُرْسِلِ السَّمَاءَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِدْرَارًا وَيَزِدْكُمْ قُوَّةً إِلَى قُوَّتِكُمْ وَلَا تَتَوَلَّوْا مُجْرِمِينَ (٥٢))
His saying (مِدْرَارًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from السَّمَاءَ; He did not make it feminine, for two reasons. The first: السَّمَاءُ here is the clouds, so مِدْرَارًا was made masculine according to the meaning. The second: mifʿāl is for intensiveness, and in that the feminine and masculine are alike, as with faʿūl, such as صَبُورٌ, and faʿīl, such as بَغِيٌّ.
(إِلَى قُوَّتِكُمْ): «إِلَى» here is construed according to the meaning, and the meaning of يَزِدْكُمْ is "He will add". It is also possible for «إِلَى» to be an adjective of قُوَّةً, so that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, i.e. "strength added to your strength".

ukberi-tibyan:54-54.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنْ نَقُولُ إِلَّا اعْتَرَاكَ بَعْضُ آلِهَتِنَا بِسُوءٍ قَالَ إِنِّي أُشْهِدُ اللَّهَ وَاشْهَدُوا أَنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِمَّا تُشْرِكُونَ (٥٤))
His saying (إِلَّا اعْتَرَاكَ): the clause explains an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "we say nothing but a saying, which is: (some of our gods) have seized you".
Its position may also be accusative, i.e. "we mention nothing but this saying".

ukberi-tibyan:57-57.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَقَدْ أَبْلَغْتُكُمْ مَا أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِ إِلَيْكُمْ وَيَسْتَخْلِفُ رَبِّي قَوْمًا غَيْرَكُمْ وَلَا تَضُرُّونَهُ شَيْئًا إِنَّ رَبِّي عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَفِيظٌ (٥٧))
His saying (فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا): i.e. تَتَوَلَّوْا; the second tāʾ was dropped.
(يَسْتَخْلِفُ): the majority read it with ḍamma, and it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the answer (that is introduced) with the fāʾ.
Some made it quiescent, (conjoining it) to the position (of the answer), or for lightening because of the succession of vowels.

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأُتْبِعُوا فِي هَذِهِ الدُّنْيَا لَعْنَةً وَيَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ أَلَا إِنَّ عَادًا كَفَرُوا رَبَّهُمْ أَلَا بُعْدًا لِعَادٍ قَوْمِ هُودٍ (٦٠))
His saying (كَفَرُوا رَبَّهُمْ): it is construed according to the meaning, i.e. "they denied their Lord".
It may also have become accusative when the bāʾ was omitted. It is also said: the implied form is "they were ungrateful for the blessing of their Lord", i.e. they were insolent about it.

ukberi-tibyan:63-63.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُ عَلَى بَيِّنَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّي وَآتَانِي مِنْهُ رَحْمَةً فَمَنْ يَنْصُرُنِي مِنَ اللَّهِ إِنْ عَصَيْتُهُ فَمَا تَزِيدُونَنِي غَيْرَ تَخْسِيرٍ (٦٣))
His saying (غَيْرَ تَخْسِيرٍ): the strongest in meaning is that «غَيْرَ» here is an exception in meaning, and it is the second object of تَزِيدُونَنِي, i.e. "you would increase me in nothing but loss". It is weak for it to be an adjective of something omitted, since the implied form would then be "you would not increase me in anything other than loss", which is the opposite of the meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:66-66.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا جَاءَ أَمْرُنَا نَجَّيْنَا صَالِحًا وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ مِنَّا وَمِنْ خِزْيِ يَوْمِئِذٍ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ الْقَوِيُّ الْعَزِيزُ (٦٦))
His saying (وَمِنْ خِزْيِ يَوْمِئِذٍ): it is read with kasra on the mīm, on the basis that it is declinable (muʿrab), its genitive being due to annexation; and with fatḥa on it, on the basis that it is indeclinable (mabnī) together with «إِذْ», because «إِذْ» is indeclinable, and an adverb of time, when annexed to something indeclinable, may be made indeclinable, because of the vagueness in adverbs, and because the muḍāf acquires many of the states of the muḍāf ilayhi, such as definiteness, interrogation, generality and conditionality.
As for «إِذْ», it has already been mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:67-67.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَخَذَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ فَأَصْبَحُوا فِي دِيَارِهِمْ جَاثِمِينَ (٦٧))
His saying (وَأَخَذَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ): concerning the omission of the (feminine) tāʾ there are three views:
The first: He separated the verb from the fāʿil (agent). The second: the femininity is not real (grammatical only). The third: الصَّيْحَةُ has the meaning of الصِّيَاحُ ("shouting"), so it was construed according to the meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:68-68.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَأَنْ لَمْ يَغْنَوْا فِيهَا أَلَا إِنَّ ثَمُودَ كَفَرُوا رَبَّهُمْ أَلَا بُعْدًا لِثَمُودَ (٦٨))
His saying (كَأَنْ لَمْ يَغْنَوْا فِيهَا): this has been mentioned in al-Aʿrāf.
(لِثَمُودَ): it is read with tanwīn, because it is masculine, being (the name of) a clan, or of the father of the tribe; and without tanwīn, as a diptote, on the basis that it is (the name of) the tribe.

ukberi-tibyan:69-69.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ جَاءَتْ رُسُلُنَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ بِالْبُشْرَى قَالُوا سَلَامًا قَالَ سَلَامٌ فَمَا لَبِثَ أَنْ جَاءَ بِعِجْلٍ حَنِيذٍ (٦٩))
His saying (بِالْبُشْرَى): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الرُّسُلُ.
(قَالُوا سَلَامًا): concerning its accusative there are two views. The first: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) according to the meaning, as though He said "they mentioned a greeting of peace". The second: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun): "be safe, safely" (أَسْلِمُوا سَلَامًا).
As for the second (سَلَامٌ), it is nominative on two views. The first: it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "my affair is peace", or "my answer", or "my saying". The second: it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is omitted, i.e. "peace be upon you".
It has also been read otherwise than this, with something whose i'rab is evident.
(أَنْ جَاءَ): concerning its position there are three views:
The first: genitive, the implied form being "from (عَنْ) coming", because لَبِثَ has the meaning of "delayed". The second: accusative, and in this there are two views: one, that when the preposition was omitted the verb reached it directly; the other, that it is construed according to the meaning, i.e. "he did not neglect bringing a calf". The third: nominative, also on two views: one, (it is) the fāʿil (agent) of لَبِثَ, i.e. "his coming was not slow"; the other, that «مَا» has the meaning of الَّذِي and is a mubtadaʾ, and «أَنْ جَاءَ» is its khabar, the implied form being "and that which Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, tarried was the measure of his coming"; or it is maṣdariyya, i.e. "his tarrying was the measure of his coming".

ukberi-tibyan:71-71.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَامْرَأَتُهُ قَائِمَةٌ فَضَحِكَتْ فَبَشَّرْنَاهَا بِإِسْحَاقَ وَمِنْ وَرَاءِ إِسْحَاقَ يَعْقُوبَ (٧١))
His saying (وَامْرَأَتُهُ قَائِمَةٌ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in «أَرْسَلْنَا».
(فَضَحِكَتْ): the majority read it with kasra on the ḥāʾ. It was also read with fatḥa on it, and the meaning is "she menstruated"; one says ضَحَكَتِ الْأَرْنَبُ ("the hare menstruated"), with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ.
(وَمِنْ وَرَاءِ إِسْحَاقَ يَعْقُوبَ): it is read in the nominative, and in this there are two views:
The first: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what precedes it is the khabar (predicate). The second: it is made nominative by the adverb (ẓarf).
It is also read with fatḥa on the bāʾ, and in this there are two views:
The first: the fatḥa here is for the accusative, and in this there are two views: one, it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the position of «بِإِسْحَاقَ»; the other, it is made accusative by an omitted verb indicated by the context, its implied form being "and We granted him, after Isḥāq, Yaʿqūb". The second view: the fatḥa is for the genitive, and it is conjoined to the wording of إِسْحَاقَ, i.e. "so We gave her glad tidings of Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb". In both views of conjunction, يَعْقُوبَ is separated from the conjoining wāw by the adverb, which is weak according to some; we have mentioned that in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:72-72.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَتْ يَا وَيْلَتَا أَأَلِدُ وَأَنَا عَجُوزٌ وَهَذَا بَعْلِي شَيْخًا إِنَّ هَذَا لَشَيْءٌ عَجِيبٌ (٧٢))
His saying (وَهَذَا بَعْلِي شَيْخًا): هَذَا is a mubtadaʾ (subject), بَعْلِي is its khabar (predicate), and شَيْخًا is an emphasizing ḥāl (circumstantial) from «بَعْلِي», since the purpose is not to inform that he is her husband in the state of his old age and not otherwise. What governs the ḥāl is the meaning of pointing and of drawing attention, or one of the two.
It is also read «شَيْخٌ» in the nominative, and in this there are several views. The first: «هَذَا» is a mubtadaʾ, «بَعْلِي» a badal (substitute) from it, and «شَيْخٌ» the khabar. The second: «بَعْلِي» is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), and «شَيْخٌ» the khabar.
The third: «بَعْلِي» is a second mubtadaʾ and «شَيْخٌ» its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of هَذَا. The fourth: «بَعْلِي» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and «شَيْخٌ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "he is an old man". The fifth: «شَيْخٌ» is a second khabar. The sixth: «بَعْلِي» and «شَيْخٌ» together are a single khabar, as we say هَذَا حُلْوٌ حَامِضٌ ("this is sweet-sour").
The seventh: «شَيْخٌ» is a badal from بَعْلِي.

ukberi-tibyan:73-73.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا أَتَعْجَبِينَ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ رَحْمَتُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ إِنَّهُ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ (٧٣))
His saying (أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ): its implied form is "O people of the house"; or it is accusative by way of extolling and specification, i.e. "I mean".
In ordinary speech it is not permitted to put something like this in the genitive as a badal (substitute), because nothing is substituted for the pronoun of the person addressed when it is perfectly clear.

ukberi-tibyan:74-74.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا ذَهَبَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ الرَّوْعُ وَجَاءَتْهُ الْبُشْرَى يُجَادِلُنَا فِي قَوْمِ لُوطٍ (٧٤))
His saying (وَجَاءَتْهُ الْبُشْرَى): it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «ذَهَبَ».
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from إِبْرَاهِيمَ, with «قَدْ» intended.
As for the answer of «لَمَّا», in it there are two views. The first: it is omitted, its implied form being "he set about disputing with Us", and on this view يُجَادِلُنَا is a ḥāl. The second: it is يُجَادِلُنَا, which is an imperfect with the meaning of the past, i.e. "he disputed with Us".
It is far-fetched for the answer to be «جَاءَتْهُ الْبُشْرَى», because that would require the wāw to be redundant, which is weak.

ukberi-tibyan:75-75.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لَحَلِيمٌ أَوَّاهٌ مُنِيبٌ (٧٥))
(أَوَّاهٌ): of the pattern faʿʿāl, from التَّأَوُّهُ ("sighing").

ukberi-tibyan:76-76.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ أَعْرِضْ عَنْ هَذَا إِنَّهُ قَدْ جَاءَ أَمْرُ رَبِّكَ وَإِنَّهُمْ آتِيهِمْ عَذَابٌ غَيْرُ مَرْدُودٍ (٧٦))
His saying (آتِيهِمْ): it is the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ, and «عَذَابٌ» is made nominative by it. It is also said: «عَذَابٌ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «آتِيهِمْ» a khabar placed first. What made that permissible is that عَذَابٌ, although indefinite, has been described by His saying «غَيْرُ مَرْدُودٍ», and that the annexation of the active participle here does not make it definite, since what is meant by it is the future.

ukberi-tibyan:77-78.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَمَّا جَاءَتْ رُسُلُنَا لُوطًا سِيءَ بِهِمْ وَضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعًا وَقَالَ هَذَا يَوْمٌ عَصِيبٌ (٧٧) وَجَاءَهُ قَوْمُهُ يُهْرَعُونَ إِلَيْهِ وَمِنْ قَبْلُ كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ السَّيِّئَاتِ قَالَ يَاقَوْمِ هَؤُلَاءِ بَنَاتِي هُنَّ أَطْهَرُ لَكُمْ فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَلَا تُخْزُونِي فِي ضَيْفِي أَلَيْسَ مِنْكُمْ رَجُلٌ رَشِيدٌ (٧٨))
His saying (سِيءَ بِهِمْ): what stands in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent) is the pronoun of Lūṭ. And «ذَرْعًا» is a tamyīz (specification).
And (يُهْرَعُونَ إِلَيْهِ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); its past is أَهْرَعَ.
(هَؤُلَاءِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject); «بَنَاتِي» is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) or a badal (substitute); «هُنَّ» is a separating pronoun (faṣl); and «أَطْهَرُ» is the khabar (predicate). It is also possible for هُنَّ to be a second mubtadaʾ and أَطْهَرُ its khabar.
It is also possible for «بَنَاتِي» to be a khabar, and «هُنَّ أَطْهَرُ» a mubtadaʾ and khabar.
It was read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, «أَطْهَرَ» in the accusative, and in this there are two views:
The first: «بَنَاتِي» is a khabar, «هُنَّ» a faṣl, and «أَطْهَرَ» a ḥāl.
The second: «هُنَّ» is a mubtadaʾ, «لَكُمْ» a khabar, and «أَطْهَرَ» a ḥāl; what governs it is the sense of emphasis in «هُنَّ» through repetition of the meaning. It is also said: what governs it is «لَكُمْ», because of the sense of settledness (istiqrār) in it.
And «الضَّيْفُ» is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as an adjective; therefore it is not made dual or plural. It has, however, come in the plural: one says أَضْيَافٌ, ضُيُوفٌ and ضِيفَانٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:79-79.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا لَنَا فِي بَنَاتِكَ مِنْ حَقٍّ وَإِنَّكَ لَتَعْلَمُ مَا نُرِيدُ (٧٩))
His saying (مَا نُرِيدُ): «مَا» may have the meaning of الَّذِي, so that it is accusative by تَعْلَمُ, which has the meaning of تَعْرِفُ ("you know, recognize").
It may also be interrogative, in the position of the accusative by نُرِيدُ; and «عَلِمْتَ» is suspended (muʿallaqa, its governing effect blocked) [Translator's note: the source says «عَلِمْتَ», though the verb in question in this phrase is «تَعْلَمُ»].

ukberi-tibyan:80-80.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ لَوْ أَنَّ لِي بِكُمْ قُوَّةً أَوْ آوِي إِلَى رُكْنٍ شَدِيدٍ (٨٠))
His saying (أَوْ آوِي): it may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf), or in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «أَنَّ» according to the meaning, its implied form being "or that I take refuge" (أَوْ أَنَّى آوِي) [Translator's note: the source as printed reads «أَنَّى»; the intended form is presumably أَنِّي].
It is weak for it to be conjoined to قُوَّةً, since if it were so it would be accusative by an implied أَنْ.
It has in fact been read so, the implied form being "or that I take refuge" (أَوْ أَنْ آوِيَ).
And (بِكُمْ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «قُوَّةً», not governed by it, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:81-81.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا يَا لُوطُ إِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَنْ يَصِلُوا إِلَيْكَ فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ وَلَا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنْكُمْ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا امْرَأَتَكَ إِنَّهُ مُصِيبُهَا مَا أَصَابَهُمْ إِنَّ مَوْعِدَهُمُ الصُّبْحُ أَلَيْسَ الصُّبْحُ بِقَرِيبٍ (٨١))
His saying (فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ): it is read with the hamza disjunctive (qaṭʿ) and conjunctive (waṣl); they are two dialectal forms: one says أَسْرَى and سَرَى.
(إِلَّا امْرَأَتَكَ): it is read in the nominative as a badal (substitute) from أَحَدٌ; the prohibition is in wording addressed to أَحَدٌ, but in meaning it is addressed to Lūṭ, i.e. "do not let any of them turn around, except your wife".
It is also read in the accusative as an exception from أَحَدٌ or from أَهْلٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:82-82.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَمَّا جَاءَ أَمْرُنَا جَعَلْنَا عَالِيَهَا سَافِلَهَا وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهَا حِجَارَةً مِنْ سِجِّيلٍ مَنْضُودٍ (٨٢))
His saying (جَعَلْنَا عَالِيَهَا): the first object, and «سَافِلَهَا» the second.
(مِنْ سِجِّيلٍ): an adjective of حِجَارَةً, and «مَنْضُودٍ» is a naʿt (adjective) of سِجِّيلٍ.
And (مُسَوَّمَةً): a naʿt of حِجَارَةً.
And (عِنْدَ): governed by مُسَوَّمَةً, or a naʿt of it.
And (هِيَ): the pronoun of the punishment.
And (بِبَعِيدٍ): a naʿt of an omitted «مَكَانٍ» ("place").
It may also be the khabar (predicate) of هِيَ; it was not made feminine because الْعُقُوبَةُ and الْعِقَابُ have one meaning, i.e. "and the punishment is not far from the wrongdoers". [Translator's note: these last phrases belong to the following verse (83): مُسَوَّمَةً عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ وَمَا هِيَ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ بِبَعِيدٍ. The source as printed reads «بِعِيدٍ».]

ukberi-tibyan:84-84.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِلَى مَدْيَنَ أَخَاهُمْ شُعَيْبًا قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مَا لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرُهُ وَلَا تَنْقُصُوا الْمِكْيَالَ وَالْمِيزَانَ إِنِّي أَرَاكُمْ بِخَيْرٍ وَإِنِّي أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ مُحِيطٍ (٨٤))
His saying (أَخَاهُمْ): the object of an omitted verb, i.e. "and We sent to Madyan". And (شُعَيْبًا) is a badal (substitute).
And (تَنْقُصُوا): it is transitive to the object by itself, and to another (object) sometimes by itself and sometimes by a preposition; you say نَقَصْتُ زَيْدًا حَقَّهُ and مِنْ حَقِّهِ ("I deprived Zayd of his right"). Here it is like that, i.e. "do not deprive the people of the measure".
It may also be transitive here to one object according to the meaning, i.e. "do not lessen and give short measure".
And (مُحِيطٍ): a naʿt (adjective) of يَوْمٍ in wording, and of الْعَذَابُ in meaning.
Some held that the implied form is "the punishment of a day whose punishment is all-encompassing"; this is far-fetched, because مُحِيطٌ would then have been applied to something other than what it belongs to, and its agent would then have to be made overt, annexed to the pronoun of the thing described.

ukberi-tibyan:87-87.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا يَا شُعَيْبُ أَصَلَاتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أَنْ نَتْرُكَ مَا يَعْبُدُ آبَاؤُنَا أَوْ أَنْ نَفْعَلَ فِي أَمْوَالِنَا مَا نَشَاءُ إِنَّكَ لَأَنْتَ الْحَلِيمُ الرَّشِيدُ (٨٧))
His saying (أَوْ أَنْ نَفْعَلَ): in the position of the accusative, conjoined to «مَا يَعْبُدُ», the implied form being "Does your prayer command you that we abandon what our fathers worship, or that we abandon doing (as we wish with our wealth)?" It is not conjoined to أَنْ نَتْرُكَ, since the meaning is not "Does your prayer command you that we do (as we wish) with our wealth?" [Translator's note: in this explanation the source writes «أَصَلَوَاتُكَ» (plural), whereas the verse as quoted reads «أَصَلَاتُكَ»; both are recognised readings.]

ukberi-tibyan:89-89.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَا قَوْمِ لَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شِقَاقِي أَنْ يُصِيبَكُمْ مِثْلُ مَا أَصَابَ قَوْمَ نُوحٍ أَوْ قَوْمَ هُودٍ أَوْ قَوْمَ صَالِحٍ وَمَا قَوْمُ لُوطٍ مِنْكُمْ بِبَعِيدٍ (٨٩))
His saying (لَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ): it is read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and with ḍamma, and this has been mentioned in al-Māʾida. Its fāʿil (agent) is «شِقَاقِي», and «أَنْ يُصِيبَكُمْ» is its second object.

ukberi-tibyan:92-92.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ أَرَهْطِي أَعَزُّ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَاتَّخَذْتُمُوهُ وَرَاءَكُمْ ظِهْرِيًّا إِنَّ رَبِّي بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ مُحِيطٌ (٩٢))
His saying (وَاتَّخَذْتُمُوهُ): it is the (verb) that is transitive to two objects, and «ظِهْرِيًّا» is the second object.
And (وَرَاءَكُمْ): it may be an adverb (ẓarf) for اتَّخَذْتُمْ, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ظِهْرِيًّا.

ukberi-tibyan:93-93.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَا قَوْمِ اعْمَلُوا عَلَى مَكَانَتِكُمْ إِنِّي عَامِلٌ سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ يَأْتِيهِ عَذَابٌ يُخْزِيهِ وَمَنْ هُوَ كَاذِبٌ وَارْتَقِبُوا إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ رَقِيبٌ (٩٣))
His saying (فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ يَأْتِيهِ): it is like the one in the story of Nūḥ, peace be upon him. [Translator's note: the source quotes «فَسَوْفَ» with fāʾ, whereas the verse here reads «سَوْفَ»; the form with fāʾ is the one in the story of Nūḥ (11:39).]

ukberi-tibyan:95-95.t:
Allah the Exalted said: {كَأَن لم يغنوا فِيهَا أَلا بعدا لمدين كَمَا بَعدت ثَمُود}
His saying (كَمَا بَعِدَتْ): it is read with kasra on the middle radical (ʿayn), its imperfect being يَبْعَدُ and the maṣdar (verbal noun) بَعَدًا, with fatḥa on the middle radical in both, i.e. "perished". It is also read with ḍamma on the middle radical, its maṣdar being الْبُعْدُ; this is from remoteness in place.

ukberi-tibyan:98-98.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَقْدُمُ قَوْمَهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فَأَوْرَدَهُمُ النَّارَ وَبِئْسَ الْوِرْدُ الْمَوْرُودُ (٩٨))
His saying (يَقْدُمُ قَوْمَهُ): it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf), with no grammatical position.
(فَأَوْرَدَهُمُ): its implied form is فَيُورِدُهُمْ ("and he will lead them"). The fāʿil (agent) of (بِئْسَ) is (الْوِرْدُ), and الْمَوْرُودُ is a naʿt (adjective) of it; the one specifically blamed (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "evil is the watering-place: the Fire".
It is also possible that الْمَوْرُودُ is the one specifically blamed.

ukberi-tibyan:100-100.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الْقُرَى نَقُصُّهُ عَلَيْكَ مِنْهَا قَائِمٌ وَحَصِيدٌ (١٠٠))
His saying (ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الْقُرَى): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). And (نَقُصُّهُ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is also possible for «ذَلِكَ» to be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), with what makes it accusative omitted, i.e. "and We relate that, (being) of the tidings of the towns". There are other views on it, which have been mentioned at His saying (ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الْغَيْبِ) in Āl ʿImrān.
(مِنْهَا قَائِمٌ): a mubtadaʾ and khabar, in the position of a ḥāl from the ḥāl, from the hāʾ in نَقُصُّهُ.
And (حَصِيدٌ): a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "and of them is (one) mown down"; it has the meaning of مَحْصُودٌ ("reaped").

ukberi-tibyan:102-102.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَذَلِكَ أَخْذُ رَبِّكَ إِذَا أَخَذَ الْقُرَى وَهِيَ ظَالِمَةٌ إِنَّ أَخْذَهُ أَلِيمٌ شَدِيدٌ (١٠٢))
His saying (إِذَا أَخَذَ): an adverb (ẓarf), and what governs it is «أَخْذُ رَبِّكَ».

ukberi-tibyan:103-103.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً لِمَنْ خَافَ عَذَابَ الْآخِرَةِ ذَلِكَ يَوْمٌ مَجْمُوعٌ لَهُ النَّاسُ وَذَلِكَ يَوْمٌ مَشْهُودٌ (١٠٣))
His saying (ذَلِكَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject); «يَوْمٌ» is its khabar (predicate), and «مَجْمُوعٌ» is an adjective of يَوْمٌ.
And (النَّاسُ) is made nominative by مَجْمُوعٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:105-105.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَ يَأْتِ لَا تَكَلَّمُ نَفْسٌ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ فَمِنْهُمْ شَقِيٌّ وَسَعِيدٌ (١٠٥))
His saying (يَوْمَ يَأْتِ): «يَوْمَ» is an adverb (ẓarf), and what governs it is an implied «تَكَلَّمُ», the implied form being "no soul will speak on it".
It is also possible that what governs it is «نَفْسٌ», and this is better.
It may also be the object of an omitted verb, i.e. "remember the day it comes", and «تَكَلَّمُ» is then an adjective of it, with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "(no soul) will speak on it", or "will speak it".
It may also be accusative by an implied أَعْنِي ("I mean").
As for the fāʿil (agent) of «يَأْتِي», it is a pronoun referring back to His saying (يَوْمٌ مَجْمُوعٌ لَهُ النَّاسُ); it does not refer back to «يَوْمَ», which is annexed to يَأْتِي, because the muḍāf ilayhi is like a part of the muḍāf, so the agent cannot be part of the word, since that would lead to annexing a thing to itself. The good (reading) is to keep the yāʾ, since there is no cause requiring its omission; but some omitted it, contenting themselves with the kasra in its place, and likened that to verse-endings (fawāṣil). Parallel to that are (مَا كُنَّا نَبْغِ) and (وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَسْرِ).
(إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ): its parallel has been mentioned in the Throne Verse (Āyat al-Kursī).

ukberi-tibyan:106-108.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ شَقُوا فَفِي النَّارِ لَهُمْ فِيهَا زَفِيرٌ وَشَهِيقٌ (١٠٦) خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالْأَرْضُ إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ رَبُّكَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ فَعَّالٌ لِمَا يُرِيدُ (١٠٧) وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ سُعِدُوا فَفِي الْجَنَّةِ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالْأَرْضُ إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ رَبُّكَ عَطَاءً غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍ (١٠٨))
His saying (لَهُمْ فِيهَا زَفِيرٌ): the clause is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and what governs it is the settledness (istiqrār) contained in «فَفِي النَّارِ», or the adverbial phrase itself. It may also be a ḥāl from النَّارِ.
(خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا): خَالِدِينَ is a ḥāl, and what governs it is «لَهُمْ» or what it is attached to.
(مَا دَامَتِ): in the position of the accusative, i.e. "for the duration of the lasting of the heavens"; and «دَامَ» here is complete (tāmma, not needing a predicate).
(إِلَّا مَا شَاءَ): concerning this exception there are two opinions:
The first: it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ). The second: it is connected (muttaṣil).
Then concerning «مَا» there are two views. The first: it has the meaning of «مَنْ» ("whoever"); the meaning on this view is that the wretched, from both the unbelievers and the believers, are in the Fire, and those of them who come out of it are the monotheists.
In the second verse, by "the happy" the monotheists are meant, but the disobedient among them enter the Fire and then come out of it. So the import of the beginning of the verse is that all the monotheists are in Paradise from the outset; then He excepted from this generality the disobedient, for they do not enter it at the outset. The second view: «مَا» is in its proper sense, and the meaning is that the wretched deserve the Fire from the moment they rise from their graves, but they are held back from being admitted to it for the duration of the Standing (al-mawqif); and the happy deserve Paradise and are held back from it for the duration of the Standing. On this view (خَالِدِينَ) is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). And «فِيهَا» in the two places is a repetition according to some, since the sentence is complete without it.
Others said: «فِيهَا» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to خَالِدِينَ and is not a repetition, while in the first (فِي) it is attached to something omitted. And (عَطَاءً) is a noun of maṣdar (ism maṣdar), i.e. "as a giving of that"; it may also be an object, because الْعَطَاءُ has the meaning of "what is given".
(سُعِدُوا): with fatḥa on the sīn, and this is the good (reading); it was also read with ḍamma on it, and this is weak. Two views have been mentioned concerning it. The first: it is on the basis of dropping the augment, i.e. أُسْعِدُوا ("they were made happy"); and its basis is their saying رَجُلٌ مَسْعُودٌ ("a man made happy").
The second: it is one of those (verbs) whose intransitive and transitive have one wording, like شَحَا فَاهُ ("he opened his mouth wide") and شَحَا فُوهُ ("his mouth opened wide"); likewise سَعِدُوا and سَعَدْتُهُ. But this is not known in the language, nor is it according to analogy.
[Translator's note: the ḍamma reading (سُعِدُوا) is that of Ḥafṣ ʿan ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī; the source's text is translated as it stands.]

ukberi-tibyan:109-109.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَا تَكُ فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِمَّا يَعْبُدُ هَؤُلَاءِ مَا يَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا كَمَا يَعْبُدُ آبَاؤُهُمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَإِنَّا لَمُوَفُّوهُمْ نَصِيبَهُمْ غَيْرَ مَنْقُوصٍ (١٠٩))
His saying (غَيْرَ مَنْقُوصٍ): a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "in full".

ukberi-tibyan:111-111.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّ كُلًّا لَمَّا لَيُوَفِّيَنَّهُمْ رَبُّكَ أَعْمَالَهُمْ إِنَّهُ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ (١١١))
His saying (وَإِنَّ كُلًّا): it is read with the nūn doubled and كُلًّا in the accusative, which is the original.
It is also read with (the nūn) lightened and (كُلًّا) in the accusative, and this is good, because «إِنَّ» is modelled on the verb, and the verb governs after omission as it governs before omission, as in لَمْ يَكُنْ and لَمْ يَكُ.
Concerning the khabar (predicate) of (إِنَّ), on both readings, there are two views. The first: «لَيُوَفِّيَنَّهُمْ».
And «مَا» is light (undoubled) and redundant (zāʾida), to serve as a separator between the lām of إِنَّ and the lām of the oath, out of dislike for their succession, just as they separated the nūns with an alif in their saying أَحْسِنَانِّ عَنِّي [Translator's note: the source as printed reads «أَحْسِنَانَّ»]. The second: the khabar is «مَا», which is indefinite, i.e. "(are) creatures" or "a group".
It is also read with the mīm doubled, with كُلًّا in the accusative, and in this there are three views. The first: the origin is لَمَنْ مَا, with kasra on the first mīm, or if you wish with fatḥa; the nūn was changed into a mīm and assimilated, then the first mīm was dropped out of dislike of repetition. Dropping the first and keeping the quiescent one was permissible because the lām is joined to it. And it is the khabar on these two implied forms. The second view: it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of لَمَّ يَلُمُّ, "to gather", but he treated continuous speech like a pause; some gave it tanwīn; its accusative is as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object pronoun in «لَيُوَفِّيَنَّهُمْ»; and this is weak. The third view: he doubled the mīm of «مَا», as the letter on which one pauses is doubled in some dialects; and this is extremely far-fetched.
It is also read «وَإِنْ» with the nūn lightened and «كُلٌّ» in the nominative, and in this there are two views. The first: it is the lightened (form of إِنَّ), its noun is omitted, and كُلٌّ with its khabar is the khabar of إِنْ; on this view «لَمَّا» is indefinite, i.e. "creatures" or "a group", as we mentioned on the accusative reading. The second: «إِنْ» has the meaning of «مَا» (negation) and «لَمَّا» has the meaning of «إِلَّا», i.e. "each one, He will surely repay them in full".
It has been read so as an irregular (shādhdh) reading. Whoever doubled (the mīm) follows what has preceded. And «لَمَّا» with doubling may not be the jussive particle, nor (the adverb meaning) "when", because the meaning would be corrupted.

ukberi-tibyan:112-112.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَاسْتَقِمْ كَمَا أُمِرْتَ وَمَنْ تَابَ مَعَكَ وَلَا تَطْغَوْا إِنَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ (١١٢))
His saying (وَمَنْ تَابَ): it is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the fāʿil (agent) in «اسْتَقِمْ»; it may also be accusative as a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment).

ukberi-tibyan:113-113.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تَرْكَنُوا إِلَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا فَتَمَسَّكُمُ النَّارُ وَمَا لَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ أَوْلِيَاءَ ثُمَّ لَا تُنْصَرُونَ (١١٣))
His saying (وَلَا تَرْكَنُوا): it is read with fatḥa on the kāf, its past on this reading being رَكِنَ, with kasra on it; this is a dialectal form. It is also said: its past on this reading has fatḥa on the kāf, but it came on the pattern faʿala yafʿalu with fatḥa in both, which is irregular. It is also said: the two dialects are intermingled; that is, one whose dialect has fatḥa [in the past] heard the fatḥa in the imperfect according to another's dialect, and pronounced it accordingly.
It is also read with ḍamma on the kāf, its past being رَكَنَ, with fatḥa on it.
(فَتَمَسَّكُمُ): the majority read it with fatḥa on the tāʾ.
It was also read with kasra on it, and this is a dialectal form. It is also said: it is a dialectal form in every (verb) whose past has kasra on its middle radical and whose final radical is the same as its middle radical, like مَسَّ, whose origin is مَسِسْتُ; they gave kasra to its first letter in the imperfect to draw attention to that.

ukberi-tibyan:114-114.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ طَرَفَيِ النَّهَارِ وَزُلَفًا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ إِنَّ الْحَسَنَاتِ يُذْهِبْنَ السَّيِّئَاتِ ذَلِكَ ذِكْرَى لِلذَّاكِرِينَ (١١٤))
His saying (طَرَفَيِ النَّهَارِ): an adverb (ẓarf) for أَقِمْ.
(وَزُلَفًا): with fatḥa on the lām, the plural of زُلْفَةٌ, like ظُلْمَةٌ and ظُلَمٌ.
It is also read with ḍamma on it, and in this there are two views:
The first: it is also the plural of زُلْفَةٌ, the lām having been quiescent, as in بُسْرَةٌ and بُسْرٌ, but he made the ḍamma follow the ḍamma. The second: it is the plural of زَلِيفٌ, which is attested.
It is also read with sukūn on the lām, and it is the plural of زُلْفَةٌ according to the original, like بُسْرَةٌ and بُسْرٌ; or it is lightened from the plural of زَلِيفٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:116-116.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَوْلَا كَانَ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ أُولُو بَقِيَّةٍ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْفَسَادِ فِي الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِمَّنْ أَنْجَيْنَا مِنْهُمْ وَاتَّبَعَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مَا أُتْرِفُوا فِيهِ وَكَانُوا مُجْرِمِينَ (١١٦))
His saying (أُولُو بَقِيَّةٍ): the majority read it with the yāʾ doubled, which is the original.
It was also read with it lightened, being the maṣdar (verbal noun) of بَقِيَ يَبْقَى بَقْيَةً, like لَقِيتُهُ لَقْيَةً. It may be in its proper sense; or it may be a maṣdar with the meaning of faʿīl, which has the meaning of fāʿil.
(فِي الْأَرْضِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْفَسَادِ.
(وَاتَّبَعَ): the majority read it with a conjunctive hamza (hamzat waṣl) and fatḥa on the tāʾ and the bāʾ, i.e. "they followed the lusts".
It was also read with ḍamma on the hamza, making it disjunctive, sukūn on the tāʾ and kasra on the bāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. وَأُتْبِعَ], the implied form being "the recompense of that in which they were given luxury".

ukberi-tibyan:119-119.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ رَبُّكَ وَلِذَلِكَ خَلَقَهُمْ وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ (١١٩))
His saying (إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ): it is excepted from the agent pronoun in «يَزَالُونَ». And «ذَلِكَ» refers back to the mercy; it is also said: to the disagreement.

ukberi-tibyan:120-120.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكُلًّا نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الرُّسُلِ مَا نُثَبِّتُ بِهِ فُؤَادَكَ وَجَاءَكَ فِي هَذِهِ الْحَقُّ وَمَوْعِظَةٌ وَذِكْرَى لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ (١٢٠))
His saying (وَكُلًّا): it is made accusative by «نَقُصُّ».
And (مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ): an adjective of كُلًّا; and «مَا نُثَبِّتُ» is a badal (substitute) from كُلًّا, or it is nominative by an implied هُوَ ("it is").
It may also be the object of «نَقُصُّ», with «كُلًّا» a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَا», or from the hāʾ, according to the school of those who permit placing the ḥāl of a genitive noun before it, or from «أَنْبَاءِ», also according to this school; and كُلًّا then has the meaning of «جَمِيعًا» ("all together").
«فِي هَذِهِ»: it is said: in this world; and it is said: in this sūra. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
If you make (هُودًا) the name of the sūra, you do not make it triptote (lā taṣrifuhu), because of definiteness and femininity. According to some, it may be made triptote because its middle letter is vowelless; according to others it may not be made triptote under any circumstances, because it is a case of naming a feminine with a masculine. If you make it the name of the Prophet, upon him be peace, you make it triptote.
Allah the Exalted said: (الر كِتَابٌ أُحْكِمَتْ آيَاتُهُ ثُمَّ فُصِّلَتْ مِنْ لَدُنْ حَكِيمٍ خَبِيرٍ (١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كِتَابٌ): i.e. "this is a Book"; and it may be the khabar (predicate) of «الر», i.e. "«الر» and the like of it are a Book".
(ثُمَّ فُصِّلَتْ): the majority read it with ḍamma and a doubled letter.
It is also read with fatḥa and a light (undoubled) letter, in the active voice; the meaning is then "then they parted", as in His saying (فَلَمَّا فَصَلَ طَالُوتُ), i.e. "departed".
(مِنْ لَدُنْ): it may be a naʿt (adjective), i.e. "being from the presence of"; and it may be an object, governed by فُصِّلَتْ.
And «لَدُنْ» is indeclinable (mabnī) even though it is put in a genitive construct, because the reason for its indeclinability is its departure from its counterpart: لَدُنْ is in the sense of عِنْدَ, but it is specific to adjoining a thing and being very close to it, whereas «عِنْدَ» is not so; rather it is for what is near and what is far from it, and in the sense of ownership.
